findings.body: The guard is dead code: `website_name` is emitted for every user, including as an explicit `website_name: nil` key when the profile has no website, instead of being omitted like every other conditionally-included attribute.
findings.failure_mode: Serializer emits the attribute unconditionally because the guard method name never matches the framework lookup.
findings.impact: The guard is dead code: `website_name` is emitted for every user, including as an explicit `website_name: nil` key when the profile has no website, instead of being omitted like every other conditionally-included attribute.
findings.root_cause: New include guard defined without the trailing `?` required by the active_model_serializers naming convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the method to `def include_website_name?` to match the AMS 0.8 convention used by all other include guards in this serializer.
findings.title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix so the serializer never invokes the include guard
findings.trigger: Serialize any user via UserSerializer; active_model_serializers 0.8 (pinned in Gemfile.lock) only consults conditional-inclusion methods named `include_<attr>?`, e.g. `include_card_image_badge_id?` elsewhere in this file.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 153 shows `def include_website_name` without trailing `?`. AMS 0.8 (confirmed in Gemfile.lock) requires `include_<attr>?` convention as seen at line 161 `def include_card_image_badge_id?`. The guard will never be invoked, causing unconditional serialization.

raw_findings.body: The website host (and path when it matches the instance domain) of a restricted TL0 profile is leaked to anonymous viewers and rendered in the profile header, defeating the existing anti-spam/privacy restriction on the `website` field.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Restricted profile data is serialized and displayed to anonymous users despite the source field being hidden.
raw_findings.impact: The website host (and path when it matches the instance domain) of a restricted TL0 profile is leaked to anonymous viewers and rendered in the profile header, defeating the existing anti-spam/privacy restriction on the `website` field.
raw_findings.root_cause: New derived attribute exposes data from the restricted `website` field without inheriting the `untrusted_attributes` scope check.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or make the include guard also return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true).
raw_findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction that hides website for TL0 users viewed anonymously
raw_findings.trigger: An anonymous visitor requests the profile of a TL0 user who has set a website; `scope.restrict_user_fields?` suppresses `website` via `untrusted_attributes`, but `website_name` is a plain attribute with no scope check (`include_website_name` only tests `website.present?`).

raw_findings.body: The most complex branch of the new `website_name` logic, including its parent-domain comparison and both ternary outcomes, ships completely unverified; regressions in that branch would pass CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested conditional logic can silently regress without any spec failure.
raw_findings.impact: The most complex branch of the new `website_name` logic, including its parent-domain comparison and both ternary outcomes, ships completely unverified; regressions in that branch would pass CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: New multi-branch serializer method landed with tests exercising only two of its three branches.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add specs where both hosts have three labels: one sharing a parent domain (expect 'www.example.com/user') and one with a different parent domain (expect the bare host).
raw_findings.title: Sibling-subdomain branch of website_name (elsif at serializer line 144-146) has no test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: The new specs stub hostnames 'discourse.org', 'example.com', and 'forums.example.com' against website 'http://example.com/user'; none of them reaches the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch (e.g. website 'http://www.example.com/user' with instance 'forum.example.com').
